result:
There's this mystique that surrounds mornings. Poets have romanticized dawn, authors have penned verses about the early hours, and motivational speakers venerate the power of embracing the day while it's still fresh and untouched. The morning sun is no less than a flaming emblem of hope, during which one can set aside yesterday's failures and embark anew towards the drawn-out tapestry of dreams and aspirations.

What makes mornings fascinating is not merely its tangible beauty; the glowing horizon, dew-kissed flowers, or the chirping birds, it's the state of the world in those hours. The world is quiet, in deep contemplation, submitting itself to the virtue of silence and tranquility. It's when the world slips into a comfortable aloofness, subtly inviting you to shed off your inhibition, your anxieties and sit down for a while, introspecting, reflecting or merely observing the world in its microcosm. Life, in its chaotic fracas, rarely affords you such moments of solitude where you can be alone with your thoughts, where you can hear your inner voice without succumbing to the cacophony of external voices. Morning, therefore, is not about seizing the day, but rather a gentle embrace of the day, a soft acceptance of all the promises and challenges it encloses within tick-tock of the clock.

On the other hand, nights have their own charm. If mornings are about hope, nights are about acceptance and closure. They are about embracing the darkness, and in that acceptance, finding your own spark. Nights are surreal and they let you escape into the labyrinth of your imagination or retrospect. It's during the night that we often find ourselves looking up at the majestic canvas of the sky studded with stars, wondering about our own insignificance in the grand design of the cosmos. The night with its enigmatic beauty makes us philosophers and poets, probing us to delve deeper into our thoughts and let the emotions flow, unregulated, uncontrolled. 

Just as the sun and the moon have their celestial dance swayed by the rhythm of the cosmos, human life, in its core, is built around this climactic alternation of day and night. Each of us can relate to either mornings or nights, and sometimes both. Magically, we associate these periods with our moods, productivity, and creativity, without perhaps realizing how beautifully this association mirrors our zest for life. 

Mornings and nights are not just slices of time but are great metaphors that encapsulate the essence of being human. Artists and thinkers from Vincent Van Gogh to Robert Frost have marveled at this dichotomy and expressed their reverence through their masterpiece paintings and poetry. Their works offer us a profound insight into the grandeur and glory of day and night and their tacit influence on our thoughts and actions. 

In a broader perspective, the cycle of day and night is no less than a symbol of life itself - with births and emptying of possibilities, ebbs and flow of strength, and the abiding rhythm of joys and sorrows. The more we learn to appreciate this cycle, the more we will resonate with the richness and depth of life, hence making the journey less of a race and more of a waltz.

People often debate over being a morning person or a night owl. But wouldn’t it be way more fulfilling if we acknowledge both? Waking up with the sun, feeling the cold wind, appreciating the start of a new day, new ideas, and opportunities. And then, winding down when the night crawls in, remembering the events of the day, embracing the peace and calm, knowing that tomorrow is another chance to do better. Because isn’t life about reminiscing cherished moments and creating new ones?

In the end, as the wise man once said - “Life is what happens to you while you're busy making other plans.” So, why not stop for a moment during our mornings or nights or whenever, just take a breath in this transient journey, keeping an eye on our ultimate destination, and at the same time, admiring the beauty that surrounds us in our sojourn.
